chunks: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father and Muhammad ibn Ismail from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan all together from Hammad ibn Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): Will you not inform me from where you knew and ruled that the wiping is of part of the head and part of the two feet? He laughed and then said: O Zurara, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) ruled it to be so and the Book from Allah descended with it — because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Wash your faces' so we understood that the entire face ... then he said: 'So we understood when He said 'with part of your heads' that the wiping is of part of the head because of the position of the letter 'Ba' (ب) ...'

key_terms.لِمَكَانِ الْبَاءِ: Because of the position/nature of the letter Ba

ai.seo_question: What is the linguistic evidence in the Quran for wiping only part of the head during ablution?
ai.summary: Zurara queries Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the jurisprudential derivation of partial wiping (masah) for the head and feet during ablution. The Imam attributes this ruling to the Prophet (PBUH) and elucidates the linguistic nuance of the preposition 'ba' (ب) in 'bi-ru'usikum', which signifies partiality, contrasting it with the comprehensive washing of the face. This hadith underscores the Shia methodology of deriving specific fiqh details from the precise grammatical structure of the Quranic verse.

en.ammaar-muslim: 10. [10/-] al-Kafi: Ali b. Ibrahim from his father AND Muhammad b. Ismail from al-Fadhl b. Shadhan all together from Hammad b. Isa from Hariz from Zurara who said:

I said to Abi Ja’far عليه السلام: will you not inform me how you knew and ruled that the wiping should only be limited to a part of the head and a part of the feet, so he laughed and then said: O Zurara – the messenger of Allah ruled it to be so and the Book from Allah descended with it – because Allah Mighty and Majestic says: “wash your faces” so we understood that the whole face … then he said: “and wipe part of your head” so we understood when He said بِرُءُوسِكُمْ that the wiping is limited to part of the head because of the (letter) ‘ب’ (Ba) …
